questions.questionText: Which data structure is essential for implementing Breadth-First Search?
questions.explanation: BFS requires FIFO order to explore vertices level by level.

questions.questionText: During BFS, the queue always contains vertices from at most how many consecutive levels?
questions.explanation: The invariant guarantees the queue holds vertices from at most two consecutive distance levels.

questions.questionText: Why must BFS maintain a visited set?
options: To avoid revisiting vertices and infinite loops
To keep track of parent nodes
questions.correctAnswer: To avoid revisiting vertices and infinite loops
questions.explanation: Without marking visited, the algorithm could loop in cycles or enqueue duplicates.

questions.questionText: In the example graph, what is the shortest path distance from A to E?
questions.explanation: The path A-B-D-E or A-C-D-E has 3 edges.

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of BFS on a graph represented with adjacency lists?
questions.explanation: Each vertex and each edge is processed a constant number of times.

questions.questionText: Using a stack instead of a queue in BFS would produce which algorithm?
questions.explanation: A LIFO stack leads to depth-first traversal.

questions.questionText: When is a vertex removed from the queue during BFS?
options: After all its neighbors are processed
When it is dequeued from the front
questions.correctAnswer: When it is dequeued from the front
questions.explanation: Dequeue operation removes the front element of the FIFO queue.

questions.questionText: In a star graph with V vertices, what is the maximum number of vertices that can be in the queue simultaneously?
questions.explanation: After processing the center, all V-1 leaves are enqueued.

questions.questionText: To visit all vertices in a disconnected graph using BFS, what must you do?
options: Run BFS once from any vertex
Run BFS for each connected component
questions.correctAnswer: Run BFS for each connected component
questions.explanation: An outer loop over all vertices ensures each component is processed.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a property of BFS?
options: Visits vertices in order of distance from source
Guarantees shortest paths in unweighted graphs
questions.explanation: BFS is iterative and uses a queue, not recursion.
